title: Pendulum length and timing
bodyMd:
Students suspended a small metal bob from a string. They released it from a small angle without pushing and timed ten complete oscillations, where one oscillation returns the bob to the same position moving in the same direction. Air currents were blocked. Each time below is the mean of three trials. The period is the time for one oscillation.

Experiment1 used the same50g bob and release angle while changing string length.

| Length (cm) | Time for ten oscillations (s) |
|---:|---:|
|25|10.0|
|50|14.2|
|100|20.0|

Experiment2 used a100cm string and the same release angle while changing bob mass.

| Mass (g) | Time for ten oscillations (s) |
|---:|---:|
|25|20.1|
|50|20.0|
|100|20.1|

The timer's reading uncertainty for each ten-oscillation interval was0.2s. One student proposed Model A: period is proportional to string length. Another proposed Model B: period is proportional to the square root of string length. Both models predict no mass effect under these conditions.
